newsitem.title: USA: California to cut off benefits to illegal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: California to cut off benefits to illegal immigrants.

text.p: California will cut off more than 200 benefits to illegal immigrants as a result of a change in federal law, Gov. Pete Wilson's office said Tuesday.

The services to be cut off to illegal immigrants include unemployment and disability insurance benefits, student financial aid, housing assistance and alcohol and drug treatment, the Wilson administration said.
It said a welfare reform law passed by Congress last year required California to eliminate many public benefits to the more than 2 million illegal immigrants Wilson says are in the state.
Wilson, a Republican who takes a tough stance against illegal immigration, ordered state agencies to prepare regulations to stop providing the benefits.
By removing many services to illegal immigrants "we are no longer rewarding those who break the law by entering the United States illegally," Wilson said in a statement.
However, Wilson said he was seeking state legislation to exempt nine public benefits from the cutoff for humanitarian reasons and to protect life, safety and public health.

Illegal immigrants will continue to be eligible for services such as care for the severely disabled and aged and for sick children. The state will pay for those services for illegal immigrants currently receiving them until alternative sources of care are found or until deportation proceedings are completed, Wilson's office said.
